🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
pkg/monitortests/network/disruptionpodnetwork/monitortest.go (1)
`136-136`: _⚡ Quick win_ **Make staged delays context-aware in `PrepareCollection`.** At lines 136, 144, 152, 160, and 174, `time.Sleep` ignores context cancellation. If `ctx` is canceled during setup (timeout or abort), these sleeps will block completion unnecessarily. Use a context-aware delay helper like `time.NewTimer` with a select statement on both the timer and `ctx.Done()` to allow prompt cancellation.
Example helper ```go func sleepWithContext(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) error { timer := time.NewTimer(d) defer timer.Stop() select { case <-timer.C: return nil case <-ctx.Done(): return ctx.Err() } } ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate. In `@pkg/monitortests/network/disruptionpodnetwork/monitortest.go` at line 136, PrepareCollection currently uses time.Sleep (at the spots where it waits during staged setup) which ignores ctx cancellation; replace each time.Sleep call in PrepareCollection with a context-aware wait using a helper like sleepWithContext(ctx, duration) that waits on a timer and selects on ctx.Done(), returning ctx.Err() on cancel. Implement sleepWithContext (as described) and propagate its error in PrepareCollection (return early if it returns non-nil) so the setup aborts promptly when ctx is canceled. ```
